maintenance.reason: Alpha9.81 fixes the post-cheap/restart MinSOC baseline contamination exposed by the 4–5 October live EV test. FoxESS ownership release is no longer considered complete merely because restore service calls returned: KEMS now keeps ownership until both Work Mode and MinSOC read back at the requested restore values. For the already-contaminated state, a narrow repair is allowed only after cheap/EV-hold/source-grace authority has genuinely ended and only when the stored baseline, live MinSOC readback and KEMS' last physically verified EV hold all match above the current normal non-cheap target; the backend then repairs the baseline to the reviewed number entity minimum (10% on the commissioned KH7). This restores the physical 10% non-cheap baseline and battery-to-home operation without changing Alpha9.75 verified hold/freeze, Alpha9.76 pending Intelligent hold or Alpha9.77 restart commissioning bridge behavior. No new FoxESS command surface, Force Discharge, import/export power-limit write, paid/Agile export control, automatic Master enable or direct Ohme charging command is added. Alpha9.80 is an immediate dashboard-loading hotfix for the Alpha9.79 runtime dashboard repair. Alpha9.79 removed an inline solar Jinja assignment from two Live Data markdown blocks but left that line's leading indentation behind, over-indenting the first markdown table row while the following separator row stayed at the normal block-scalar indentation. Home Assistant therefore parsed the separator as a YAML block-scalar token and failed to load /config/kems_master_dashboard.yaml. Alpha9.80 restores the correct markdown indentation in both runtime Live Data blocks and adds a regression that applies the runtime dashboard repair to the managed Master dashboard and YAML-parses the resulting payload. This release changes no FoxESS, EV, tariff, optimiser, commissioning, ROI arithmetic or hardware-write authority. Alpha9.79 reconciles the managed Master and ROI dashboards with the entity IDs KEMS actually registers. It adds a first-class Observed solar generation today sensor backed by the canonical actual daily solar total; replaces stale lifetime gas/cost and financial-commissioning entity names with their current registered equivalents; updates the simulated battery charged-today reference; and removes the dead Agile rolling-export-plan sensor dependency by deriving the current plan directly from the existing Agile slot payload. A new regression contract audits explicit KEMS entity references in the managed Master/ROI dashboards against KEMS entity declarations so future dashboard/entity drift fails CI. This release is presentation/reporting/entity-surface only: it does not change FoxESS, EV, optimiser, tariff, commissioning or hardware-write authority. Alpha9.78 moves the external EV state-of-charge sync automation into KEMS as an explicitly opt-in, narrowly bounded Ohme write path. KEMS auto-discovers a Stellantis vehicle battery percentage source and the Ohme state-of-charge input number, refreshes immediately when the vehicle SOC or EV connection state changes, and writes only number.set_value while the EV is connected, the source/target values are valid, KEMS emergency stop is clear, the values differ by at least 0.5 percentage points and the write cooldown has expired. Every evaluation/write retains diagnostic audit evidence including source/target entities and values, trigger, requested value, immediate readback, result, timestamps and attempt/success/failure counts. This does not start or stop EV charging, does not change Ohme charge mode, does not broaden FoxESS/export authority, and is disabled by default until the KEMS EV SOC sync switch is explicitly enabled. Alpha9.77 closes the restart commissioning gap live-proven on 3 October 2026. Raw FoxESS physical commissioning samples remain session-scoped and are rebuilt after every restart. KEMS now persists only a compact identity-bound certificate after a fresh session has passed the full telemetry-stability, battery-direction and whole-site power-balance proof. On a later HA/KEMS restart that certificate may temporarily satisfy only those three time-based WAIT checks while fresh samples rebuild, and only when the current authoritative source entity/unit fingerprint and direction-evidence fingerprint exactly match the stored proof and the configured battery power sign convention is unchanged. The bridge also requires the current post-restart samples to be non-contradictory: telemetry complete, no wrong-sign battery evidence, and every currently eligible whole-site power-balance sample balanced. The bridge never converts FAIL to PASS, never bypasses unavailable or mismatched physical sources, mapping/unit/grid-direction/command-surface checks, exact foxess_modbus version and backend gates, explicit Commissioned/Master controls, emergency/island/grid safety, tariff confirmation, SOC/site-import protections, or export authority. Fresh observations continue rebuilding in parallel and replace the bridge once the session proof is complete. Alpha9.77 does not broaden FoxESS write authority, does not add Force Discharge, paid/Agile export control, direct Ohme commands, import/export-limit writes or automatic Master enable. Alpha9.76 closes the live Intelligent extra-slot publication gap proven on 1 October 2026. When the raw Octopus Intelligent signal is already ON and fresh, Ohme positively reports the EV connected and actively charging, cheap-rate evidence is corroborated, and the only missing confirmation is the Intelligent start/end window, KEMS may immediately apply a hold-only Self Use + SOC+1 MinSOC protection using the existing reviewed FoxESS command surface. This pending Intelligent hold requires fresh physical battery SOC and, when a site-import limit is configured, fresh grid/battery power proving that replacing battery discharge with grid import stays within the configured limit. It never marks the period cheap, never authorises Force Charge, never enables paid/export control, and never broadens Ohme or import/export-limit authority. The configured next_offpeak_start and offpeak_end entities now also trigger immediate coordinator refreshes, so the normal confirmed Alpha9.75 EV hold is promoted as soon as Octopus publishes the complete window. If the slot/window evidence becomes explicitly contradictory, the pending hold releases through the existing 10% baseline path. A pending hold may be frozen across transient backend-readiness loss only with a live physical MinSOC readback at or above the pending floor; historical verification from an earlier completed session cannot prove a new pending hold. Alpha9.75 requires a physically verified FoxESS MinSOC readback before an EV hold may be reported as frozen. A fresh readback below the latched floor blocks freeze even if an older verification exists; only an unavailable readback may fall back to the persisted last verified Self Use hold. Alpha9.75 also adds a 90-second hold-only grace for temporary unknown/unavailable Ohme or Intelligent authority sources after a positively confirmed cheap EV session, plus one bounded 2-second follow-up coordinator refresh after each critical source transition so related Home Assistant states can settle. The grace issues no new FoxESS writes, does not create new cheap-period authority, never freezes Force Charge, and releases immediately on explicit EV disconnect, explicit usable non-cheap state, No Paid Export exit, Control/Master/commissioning opt-out, emergency stop, island/grid loss, or grace expiry. An unverified grace state issues no write and explicitly claims no physical protection. Alpha9.74 preserves an already-applied confirmed-cheap EV MinSOC hold across transient FoxESS/telemetry or commissioning-readiness loss without new writes, but only when the last successfully applied physical action was Self Use. While KEMS still owns FoxESS, No Paid Export remains active, cheap authority remains positively confirmed, the EV has not explicitly disconnected, Control/Master/commissioning remain enabled, and no emergency/island/grid-loss condition is active, the backend now freezes the last verified Self Use + MinSOC state instead of restoring the pre-KEMS 10% baseline. The persisted hold is revalidated/reasserted on the first normal usable cycle. Active Force Charge is never frozen across loss of safe control authority. Explicit cheap end, EV disconnect, No Paid Export exit, control opt-out, emergency stop, island/grid loss or an unmanaged Force Charge state retain the existing release path. Alpha9.74 adds no new Force Charge, Force Discharge, Ohme, import/export-limit or Master-enable authority. The retained Alpha8.74 house-first day-rate import-floor contract remains unchanged. Alpha9.73 removes the normal coordinator-poll delay from EV battery protection. Changes to the configured Ohme status/connected/charging entities and Octopus Intelligent/off-peak binary sources now request an immediate KEMS refresh, while the existing Alpha9.72 tariff confirmation, physical SOC, site-import headroom, commissioning, Master-enable, island, emergency-stop and FoxESS v1.15.0 write gates remain authoritative. This does not pre-authorise an Intelligent extra slot, does not add any new FoxESS or Ohme command surface, and does not change the normal analysis scan interval. It only shortens the time between Home Assistant publishing a genuine EV/tariff transition and the already-reviewed Alpha9.72 control path evaluating it. Alpha9.72 makes the continuously recalculated forecast-required morning SOC the canonical No Paid Export overnight charge target for both customer presentation and the existing confirmed-cheap physical Force Charge path. The target is now published throughout the day, while the legacy learned-load target remains a fail-safe fallback only when the forecast target is unavailable. Alpha9.72 also pre-arms the existing whole-bus EV MinSOC hold whenever an EV is connected during a confirmed cheap window, before Ohme reports non-zero charging power; the pre-arm changes only the already-reviewed MinSOC floor and preserves any independently safe cheap battery-charge request. The hold remains latched while the EV stays connected during the cheap window and still restores the pre-KEMS baseline when cheap authority ends or the EV disconnects. No new Force Discharge, Ohme, import/export-limit, Master-enable or commissioning authority is added; unrelated routing/optimiser state unchanged. Alpha9.71 prevents paid-grid battery charging outside confirmed cheap periods by separating the KEMS planning reserve from the physical FoxESS MinSOC-on-grid command. In live No Paid Export Self Use, KEMS now preserves the pre-KEMS MinSOC-on-grid baseline instead of raising it to the normal planning reserve; if that baseline cannot be preserved, the write fails closed. Confirmed-cheap Force Charge and Alpha9.70 EV battery-hold MinSOC authority are unchanged, so the retained whole-bus EV fallback can still raise MinSOC only while a cheap period is genuinely confirmed. No new Force Discharge, import/export-limit, Ohme, Master-enable or commissioning authority is added. Alpha9.70 adds an explicit conditional LIVE no-paid-export EV battery-hold guard during confirmed cheap windows, using only the previously reviewed Self Use, confirmed-cheap Force Charge and MinSOC-on-grid authority after existing technical commissioning and manual Master enable. It conservatively budgets Ohme once against whole-site import when load membership is unknown, inhibits charge on stale EV/site evidence, and retains a non-decreasing physical SOC hold floor across scans and HA restart. The EV and house may BOTH import cheap grid under this whole-bus fallback: there is no new house-only AC output limiter, no proof of per-circuit isolation, no new Force Discharge or import/export limit writes, and no automatic control enable. A new diagnostic sensor and persisted session state distinguish proposed hold from actual command permission. The independently modelled split remains shadow-only pending separately verified KH7 output-control and real electrical commissioning (issue #297). Alpha9.69 adds a shadow-only No Paid Export cheap-period SOC-floor and EV shared-bus allocation proposal plus read-only evidence from existing Ohme, FoxESS and Octopus telemetry. Crucially the Alpha9.68 Control-mode cheap-period planner and its already reviewed conditional physical Self Use, Force Charge and Min SoC-on-grid authority remain unchanged. The separate Alpha9.69 proposal never goes to FoxESS/Ohme command backends, and its sticky shadow-only barrier still rejects an accidental write after downstream overlays. The physical Control mode retains the Alpha9.68 learned load forecast, charge target and cheap import-headroom calculation independently of the EV-excluded twin. A bounded persistent event trace captures charging start/stop and tariff transitions at the existing coordinator scan interval with Ohme/FoxESS/grid readings and labelled mode/MinSOC readbacks for supervised commissioning; no new hardware write is enabled. Existing KEMS diagnostic sensors and retained five-minute snapshots now show measured EV net allocation and source freshness, not physical circuit isolation. No new KH7 output control, deliberate Force Discharge, import/export power-limit or paid-export writes are enabled. The distinct target-limited below-floor and concurrent EV-grid/house-battery routing require a future separately commissioned change. Alpha9.68 adds date-aware electricity tariff fallbacks without changing live Octopus authority. The existing tariff remains effective through 30 September 2026. From 1 October 2026 the scheduled fallback removes the former 5% VAT from the current tariff (day 26.9558095238p/kWh, off-peak 3.326952381p/kWh, standing charge 51.147p/day). From 4 October 2026 the renewed fallback becomes day 37.17p/kWh, off-peak 8.00p/kWh and standing charge 55.52p/day. Automatic mode continues to prefer live Home Assistant Octopus values whenever they are available; scheduled values are used only for fallback/manual resolution and as the expected cheap-rate reference for confirmed Intelligent extra-slot corroboration. Both future changes are stored as effective-dated options and do not affect September operation. Alpha9.67 makes fresh physical battery SOC authoritative for no-paid-export cheap-period charging. The solar-aware no-export target remains forecast-derived, but simulated SOC and simulated battery charge power can no longer suppress a real Force Charge request when the physical battery is below that target. Charging uses the configured maximum only as a request and remains capped by available site-import headroom; once physical SOC reaches the target KEMS returns to Self Use and holds with Min SoC-on-grid. If a usable physical SOC or target is unavailable, KEMS does not authorise battery charge. Intelligent-slot confirmation, commissioning, stale-data, island/EPS, emergency-stop, ownership/restoration and exact foxess_modbus v1.15.0 gates remain unchanged. Deliberate/economic Force Discharge, Agile/paid-export control, Import Power Limit writes and Export Power Limit writes remain blocked. Alpha9.66 removes the abandoned daytime anti-import Force Discharge experiment and restores the bounded non-Agile live-control surface to Self Use outside confirmed cheap periods, confirmed-cheap Force Charge, and Min SoC-on-grid only. No grid-bias controller, fixed export trim, measured-grid feedback loop, Import Power Limit write, or Export Power Limit write exists in the current live path. Deliberate/economic Force Discharge and Agile/paid-export control remain blocked. Existing commissioning, exact foxess_modbus v1.15.0, stale-data, island, emergency-stop, ownership, restoration, SOC and site-safety gates remain authoritative. Cheap-period logic is intentionally unchanged in this release so Intelligent extra-slot detection and charging can be tested independently. Historical retained release notes follow: Alpha9.65 replaces the closed-loop grid trim with a deterministic fixed 50 W non-economic daytime export bias. Outside confirmed cheap periods, when Control, commissioning, safety, grid availability, battery reserve and headroom gates pass, KEMS requests the already-bounded KH7 house-support AC target plus exactly 0.050 kW. There is no measured-grid feedback, no 5-second fast trim loop, no error/deadband/slew controller, and the previous user-tunable 0-100 W bias option is removed; legacy stored values are ignored and runtime policy is fixed at 50 W. Cheap periods and confirmed Intelligent charging continue to suppress the bias. Deliberate/economic export is a separate higher-priority authority: when Agile export is introduced, that export request suppresses the 50 W bias and is never stacked with it. Alpha9.65 does not write FoxESS Import Power Limit or Export Power Limit; both remain untouched. All existing commissioning, exact foxess_modbus v1.15.0, SOC reserve, inverter/discharge/export headroom, island, stale-data, emergency-stop, ownership and restoration gates remain authoritative. Alpha9.64 adds a fast FoxESS grid-trim loop while the 60-second planner remains authoritative. A 5-second scheduler only acts once per fresh FoxESS grid telemetry sample and only while the main planner has already authorised and applied the bounded No paid export Force Discharge trim. Each fresh sample adjusts the current Force Discharge total-output setpoint by signed grid error, moves at most 50 W per fresh sample, and remains inside a +/-100 W envelope around the latest planner target with the existing 5 W deadband. The fast loop cannot enter Force Discharge independently, never changes Work Mode, never writes Export Power Limit, suspends on cheap/Intelligent signals, reserve loss or withdrawn control gates, and expires if the main planner does not renew authority. All existing commissioning, exact foxess_modbus v1.15.0, island, stale-data, emergency-stop, headroom and No paid export gates remain authoritative. Deliberate/economic Force Discharge, Agile/paid-export control and Export Power Limit writes remain blocked. Alpha9.63 closes the Alpha9.62 near-zero-grid trim loop on measured grid error. The configured Grid import prevention bias remains the desired grid target (for example -10 W), while KEMS now calculates correction = observed grid power - target grid power and adds that bounded correction to the existing KH7 AC-output target. Correction is capped at 100 W, rate-limited to 50 W per control scan, held through a 5 W error deadband, and still exits to Self Use on material natural export. The existing +/-100 W planner window, SOC reserve, inverter/discharge headroom, cheap-period, island, stale-data, emergency-stop, commissioning, No paid export and exact foxess_modbus v1.15.0 gates remain authoritative. Deliberate/economic Force Discharge, Agile/paid-export control and Export Power Limit writes remain blocked. Alpha9.62 promotes the optional Grid import prevention bias into a bounded live No paid export control path. When every existing control/commissioning gate passes and the reviewed FoxESS Force Discharge command is uniquely available, KEMS may use remote Force Discharge only for near-zero-grid trimming: the FoxESS active-power setpoint is the already-bounded desired total KH7 AC output plus the configured tiny bias, rather than incorrectly commanding the bias wattage as the inverter's whole output. The live trim enters on at least 5 W import, remains engaged around the -10 W target, and releases back to Self Use once natural export reaches 50 W, while the existing +/-100 W planner trim window, SOC reserve, inverter/discharge headroom, cheap-period, island, stale-data, emergency-stop and no-paid-export gates remain authoritative. Deliberate/economic Force Discharge, Agile/paid-export control and Export Power Limit writes remain blocked. Alpha9.61 fixes Intelligent extra-slot confirmation when the battery is already supporting an actively charging EV. A genuine Octopus Intelligent slot inside its active window, with Ohme connected and actively charging above the confirmation threshold, is no longer vetoed merely because observed grid demand is lower than the EV charging load. Grid-demand corroboration remains visible as diagnostic evidence but is no longer an authority gate, preventing Self Use from draining the battery into the EV during a genuine extra cheap slot. Price, slot-window and Ohme evidence remain fail-closed, and the existing bounded FoxESS write scope is unchanged. Alpha9.60 fixes no-paid-export cheap-period target authority. Physical No paid export Control now uses the live no-export simulation rather than the Full KEMS export-capable rolling target. It charges only to the solar-aware overnight target, then holds the battery with Min SoC-on-grid while cheap grid supplies home/EV demand. Full KEMS counterfactual simulation remains unchanged and the existing bounded FoxESS write scope remains unchanged. Alpha9.59 fixes the final opt-in reload loop exposed by the first live commissioning trial. Turning Commissioned for control ON and turning Master control enable ON now persist those two explicit control gates in place and request a normal coordinator refresh instead of reloading the integration, so the current-session FoxESS commissioning evidence that authorised the action is not discarded. The OFF paths keep the existing reload/shutdown behaviour so KEMS-owned FoxESS state is still restored fail-closed when either gate is withdrawn. Master enable also refuses activation unless technical commissioning is currently ready, Commissioned for control is already ON, and KEMS Mode is Control. This is control-gate lifecycle hardening only: it does not broaden FoxESS write authority, does not enable Agile or paid export control, does not make Force Discharge or Export Power Limit writes live, and leaves the 10 W grid-import-prevention bias Shadow-only. Alpha9.58 improves FoxESS battery-direction commissioning so large batteries no longer depend solely on a whole-percentage SOC step. Direction proof remains fresh-session and fail-closed, but now prefers authoritative read-only BMS remaining-energy movement, then same-device daily charge/discharge energy counters, and only then falls back to SOC movement, while still requiring battery power above the existing 0.25 kW threshold and multiple consistent evidence samples. Source identity or unit changes, restart, or loss of the physical mapping gate reset the auxiliary evidence window. This is commissioning/read-only evidence only: it does not broaden FoxESS write authority, does not enable Agile or paid export control, does not make Force Discharge or Export Power Limit writes live, and leaves the 10 W grid-import-prevention bias Shadow-only. Alpha9.57 fixes the first-refresh startup regression exposed immediately after installing Alpha9.56: the canonical commissioning compatibility wrappers now accept and forward the provisional data_override payload used by the coordinator before coordinator.data exists, and tariff reconciliation reads that same provisional snapshot. The Alpha9.47 diagnostics compatibility layer is also pass-through for the new keyword and no longer overwrites the current bounded-control commissioning wording with the obsolete pre-control hard-block message. This is a startup/compatibility hotfix only; it does not broaden FoxESS write authority, does not enable Agile or paid export control, does not make Force Discharge or Export Power Limit writes live, and leaves the 10 W grid-import-prevention bias Shadow-only. Alpha9.56 introduces the first bounded opt-in real FoxESS control backend for non-Agile operation. Live writes are limited to Self Use, confirmed-cheap-period Force Charge and Min SoC-on-grid on the uniquely bound authoritative FoxESS device, and only when Control mode, Master control enable, the separate Commissioned for control acknowledgement, full control-critical commissioning readiness, a fresh safe plan, the complete KEMS preflight suite, on-grid operation, no emergency stop, No paid export mode and the exact reviewed foxess_modbus v1.15.0 contract all pass together. Before taking ownership KEMS persists the pre-control local FoxESS work mode and Min SoC-on-grid, and losing any authority gate releases KEMS ownership and restores those values. Deliberate Force Discharge, paid or Agile economic export control, the Alpha9.55 Grid import prevention bias and FoxESS Export Power Limit writes remain outside the live-control scope; the 10 W bias remains Shadow-only because the reviewed FoxESS remote active-power command is an inverter active-power setpoint rather than a proven net-grid-power target. Overall reporting data quality is informational for control commissioning and cannot by itself unlock writes; the control-critical FoxESS unit, telemetry-stability, battery-direction, grid-direction, whole-site power-balance, tariff, planner, limit, emergency-stop and unique command-surface evidence remains fail-closed. Alpha9.56 does not broaden Ohme authority and does not enable Agile tariff export control. Alpha9.55 adds an optional user-selected Grid import prevention bias from 0 to 100 W, with a safe default of 0 W disabled. When KEMS would otherwise sit near zero grid exchange, the Shadow control path may model a tiny export trim such as 10 W to avoid a few watts of standing grid import. This bias is operational trim rather than paid or economic export: No paid export still values export income at zero and normal economic battery-export authority remains disabled. The bias is suppressed in Observe, emergency stop, stale or unsafe plans, island/EPS operation, cheap charging, deliberate economic export, at or below the active SOC reserve, outside the +/-100 W grid trim window, or when KEMS export, inverter or discharge headroom is insufficient. Command Shadow exposes the configured bias, target and observed grid power, active or suppressed state and suppression reason, and represents an active bias as a tiny Force Discharge/export-limit proposal while commands_permitted remains false and real FoxESS hardware writes remain blocked. Alpha9.55 does not enable Control, commissioning completion, a real backend or any FoxESS hardware write. Alpha9.54 separates the user-selected KEMS export ceiling from the FoxESS installer/current hardware export ceiling. The dedicated read-only FoxESS export-limit sensor is now treated as independent hardware-maximum evidence rather than a value that must equal the KEMS setting: a KEMS ceiling at or below the observed FoxESS hardware ceiling passes commissioning compatibility, a KEMS ceiling above the observed hardware ceiling fails closed, and a missing, ambiguous or unusable authoritative readback waits rather than guessing. The effective physical export ceiling is the lower of the KEMS user ceiling and the observed FoxESS hardware ceiling. Command Shadow independently applies that lower effective ceiling to both the proposed FoxESS export-power limit and deliberate Force Discharge power. A user-selected KEMS ceiling of 0 kW is valid and means never deliberately export. The proven live case FoxESS 14.5 kW / KEMS 6.4 kW therefore resolves to an effective 6.4 kW ceiling without changing the installer setting. No-paid-export operation still proposes a transient 0 W export limit and no Force Discharge, while Full-KEMS counterfactual simulation remains separate. Alpha9.54 does not enable Control, commissioning completion, a real backend or any FoxESS hardware write; ready_for_control remains false, commands remain blocked and Simulate remains read-only. Alpha9.53 introduced the dedicated read-only FoxESS export-limit commissioning proof and remains retained as the readback/binding foundation for this revised authority model. Alpha9.52 fixes the Shadow/physical control authority boundary exposed by live Alpha9.51 diagnostics. The Full-KEMS rolling optimiser remains authoritative for counterfactual simulation and may continue to model profitable battery export, but the physical ControlState now projects that target through live export permission and island state before it can become FoxESS command intent. No-paid-export or island operation clamps deliberate physical battery export to 0 kW while preserving house-support discharge, and the FoxESS command shadow independently fails closed if deliberate export is ever presented while grid export is disabled. The configured 6.4 kW physical/DNO export capability remains reported separately from the active 0 W no-export command allowance. Alpha9.52 does not enable Control, commissioning, a real backend, or any FoxESS hardware write; all existing command and commissioning gates remain closed and Simulate remains read-only. Alpha9.51 retains a bounded deduplicated history of completed Power Down sessions, exposes every completed session for the current local day on the managed KEMS dashboard, restores an explicit Power Down event-credit row to KEMS Daily costs, and makes retained completed-event bonus evidence authoritative for completed same-day customer reporting instead of continuing to show a stale in-event estimate. Completed-event figures remain KEMS retained results rather than supplier-settled Octopus cash. Alpha9.51 is reporting, persistence and presentation only: no Power Down joining, optimiser or dispatch decisions, tariff or SOC policy, commissioning, control eligibility, Ohme authority or FoxESS hardware-write authority changes; real hardware writes remain hard-blocked. Retained successor contracts include the Alpha9 coordinated parity baseline; Alpha9.13 forecast-aware scheduling; Alpha9.19 runtime Recorder hygiene; Alpha9.20 ShadowValidationRecorder Recorder hygiene; the Alpha9.22 startup hotfix at build_slot_flow for the unexpected planning_target_soc_percent keyword; the Alpha9.24 flow parity export-floor correction with its 15% planning/export target, independent 10% absolute floor and restart-safe 12% recovery latch; Alpha9.25 observability and reporting-only 7.0 kW cheap-window charge capability; Alpha9.27 reporting-only policy-label publication; Alpha9.28 staggered V2 flow while V1 remains unchanged and no optimiser behaviour changes; Alpha9.29 extra gap V2 packet spacing while V1 remains unchanged and no optimiser behaviour changes; Alpha9.30 solar-only commissioning; Alpha9.37 canonical current-day KEMS cost dashboard parity as presentation/reporting only with no FoxESS command/write authority changes; Alpha9.44 dashboard/observability only for Weekend Happy Hour with no Happy Hour scoring or joining logic changes and no FoxESS hardware-write authority change; Alpha9.45 reward normalisation where raw 6 reports 3 rewards rather than 6, the two-one-hour-reward event-day limit and 16 kWh-per-reward-hour cap, and it does not broaden external Octopus booking authority or FoxESS hardware-write authority; Alpha9.46 Solar Generation Today authority with telemetry gaps retained as discrepancy evidence; Alpha9.48 physical daily authority for Load Energy Today, Grid Consumption Today and Feed-in Today; Alpha9.49 Power Down dashboard/observability with joining unchanged and FoxESS hardware-write authority unchanged; and Alpha9.50 final managed dashboard composition preserving Weekend Happy Hour and Power Down presentation. All prior Alpha9 safety, reporting and control contracts remain retained.
